chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad informed me, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from Abī Hammām, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام.
Regarding wudu (ablution), what is obligatory in the Book of Allah, Exalted is He, is wiping, while washing in wudu (ablution) is for cleanliness.

key_terms.الْغَسْلُ: washing, mentioned here in connection with cleanliness
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةُ: the obligatory duty mandated by Allah
key_terms.الْمَسْحُ: wiping, the prescribed act in this ruling
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before acts of worship
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah, meaning the Qur'an
key_terms.لِلتَّنْظِيفِ: for cleaning or purification of dirt

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام say is obligatory in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام distinguishes between what is obligatory in wudu (ablution) according to the Book of Allah and what serves the purpose of cleanliness. It indicates that the obligatory element is masḥ (wiping), while ghusl (washing) in wudu is associated with cleansing.
